data.name: IDS_PERMISSION_CONFIG_EMPTY
data.value: The permission configuration is empty: no operation entry rule was declared, and neither NoOperationCodes / NoModels was asserted nor a scanning assembly was given. Use OnAttribute / OnMethodName / OnAttributeOrName to declare the entry rule when there are method-level permission codes; assert NoOperationCodes when there are none; use AddPermissionModels when you only want to extend the scanning scope; assert NoModels when the application really has no permission model and no declaration.

data.name: IDS_PERMISSION_CONFIG_CONTRADICTS_CODES
data.value: The permission configuration contradicts itself: NoOperationCodes was asserted (no method-level permission codes) yet operation entry rules were declared. Only one of the two is allowed: declare rules when there are method-level permission codes, assert NoOperationCodes when there are none.

data.name: IDS_PERMISSION_CONFIG_CONTRADICTS_MODELS
data.value: The permission configuration contradicts itself: NoModels was asserted (no permission model and no declaration) yet scanning assemblies were given. Do not assert NoModels when there are assemblies to scan.

data.name: IDS_PERMISSION_CONFIG_CONTRADICTS_SOURCE
data.value: The permission configuration contradicts itself: a permission code source was specified (Source) yet operation entry rules were declared. The two are mutually exclusive source shapes: the source itself answers which permission codes a type declares for an operation, and entry rules are just one of its implementations.

data.name: IDS_PERMISSION_NO_ASSEMBLY_SCANNED
data.value: AddPermission was called without any assembly to scan. Both permission models and [Permission] declarations come from assembly scanning: an empty scanning scope silently disables row-level data scope, and the start-up validation short-circuits as well because nothing was declared. Pass the assemblies to scan, for example AddPermission(source, typeof(X).Assembly); if the application really has no permission model and no [Permission] declaration, assert services.AssertNoPermissionModels() explicitly.

data.name: IDS_PERMISSION_SUBJECT_RESOLVER_NOT_REGISTERED
data.value: A permission model or [Permission] permission code was declared, but {0} is not registered. Permission codes and row-level grants must be resolved from authorization data in real time (freezing them into a token lets a revoked permission survive in stale tokens). Please register an implementation backed by authorization data, for example services.AddScoped<{0}, YourResolver>().

data.name: IDS_PERMISSION_USER_PRINCIPAL_NOT_REGISTERED
data.value: A permission model or [Permission] permission code was declared, but {0} is not registered. The evaluation subject is taken from UserPrincipal, so resolving IScopeGuard fails outright when it is not registered. Please supply the current user principal in the service registrations.

data.name: IDS_OPERATION_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_INVALID
data.value: The entry attribute type must be a non-null attribute type (a subclass of Attribute).

data.name: IDS_OPERATION_RULE_REQUIRED
data.value: No operation entry rule was declared. Call OnAttribute / OnMethodName / OnAttributeOrName / OnMethod at least once; if the application really has no method-level permission codes, assert it explicitly with AddPermission(EmptyCodeSource.Instance, …); to only extend the assemblies to scan, use AddPermissionModels.

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_OPERATIONS_NODE_MISSING
data.value: The permission rule configuration is missing the '{0}' node (the section '{1}' was checked). Please pass the section that holds the rules, for example configuration.GetSection("Permission").

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_OPERATION_DUPLICATE_CASE
data.value: The operation name '{0}' in the configuration differs from an earlier operation only by case. Operation names are case-sensitive, please unify the spelling.

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_OPERATION_NO_RULES
data.value: The operation '{0}' in the configuration declares no entry rule: give '{1}' (an array of entry attribute type names) or '{2}' (an array of entry method names); both may be given (an entry when either one matches).

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_NO_OPERATIONS
data.value: The '{0}' node of the permission rule configuration holds no operation at all. If the application really has no method-level permission codes, assert it explicitly with AddPermission(EmptyCodeSource.Instance, …); to only extend the scanning scope, use AddPermissionModels.

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_NODE
data.value: The operation '{0}' in the configuration contains an unknown node '{1}'. Available nodes: '{2}' (entry attribute type names) and '{3}' (entry method names).

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_VALUE_MUST_BE_ARRAY
data.value: The '{0}' in the configuration must be written as an array (for example "{1}": ["…"]), not as a single string.

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_VALUE_EMPTY
data.value: The '{0}' in the configuration must be a non-empty string.

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_TYPE_UNRESOLVED
data.value: The entry attribute type '{0}' ({1}) in the configuration cannot be resolved. Please use the full type name (namespace + type name), an assembly-qualified name ("Type, Assembly"), or give the method name directly through '{2}'.

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_TYPE_GENERIC
data.value: The entry attribute type '{0}' in the configuration is a generic type: generic attributes cannot serve as entry markers.

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_TYPE_NOT_ATTRIBUTE
data.value: The entry attribute type '{0}' in the configuration is not an attribute (it should point at a subclass of Attribute).

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_TYPE_LOAD_FAILED
data.value: The entry attribute type '{0}' ({1}) in the configuration cannot be resolved: {2}

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_TYPE_AMBIGUOUS
data.value: The entry attribute type '{0}' ({1}) in the configuration matches multiple types with the same name in the scanning scope ({2}). Please use an assembly-qualified name ("Type, Assembly").

data.name: IDS_CONFIG_TYPE_SHORT_NAME_AMBIGUOUS
data.value: The entry attribute type '{0}' ({1}) in the configuration has an ambiguous short name in the scanning scope ({2}). Please use the full type name.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_OPERATION_RESERVED_PREFIX
data.value: The operation name '{0}' uses the framework-reserved prefix '{1}'. The default policy key of an operation is derived from that prefix, so the operation name itself must not carry it.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_CODE_RESERVED_PREFIX
data.value: The permission code '{0}' uses the framework-reserved prefix '{1}'. Please use a code without that prefix.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_DUPLICATE_DECLARED
data.value: The policy for permission code '{0}' is declared more than once.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_MULTIPLE_POLICY_CODES
data.value: The operation {1} on resource type '{0}' resolves to multiple permission codes that declared a row-level policy ({2}). Please make sure at most one permission code of an operation declares a policy.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_ALL_EMPTY
data.value: All needs at least one sub-policy; "unconstrained" must be written explicitly as Where(_ => true).

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_ALL_NULL
data.value: The sub-policies of All can not be null.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_ANY_EMPTY
data.value: Any needs at least one sub-policy; "unconstrained" must be written explicitly as Where(_ => true).

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_ANY_NULL
data.value: The sub-policies of Any can not be null.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_DENY_NOT_NESTABLE
data.value: Deny can not be nested. Deny means "veto", not boolean negation; use Where(x => !...) when negation is meant.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_DIMENSION_DUPLICATED
data.value: The dimension '{0}' is declared more than once in the permission model of type '{1}'.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_CLASSIFICATION_DUPLICATED
data.value: The classification '{0}' is declared more than once in the permission model of type '{1}'.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_MODEL_NO_DIMENSION
data.value: The permission model '{0}' declares no dimension at all: call ScopeModelBuilder.Map at least once (use MapMany when the value comes from a child table).

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_DIMENSION_NOT_MAPPED
data.value: The scope policy of resource type '{0}' references the unmapped dimension '{1}'. Please call Map("{1}", ...) in Define of the permission model (use MapMany("{1}", ...) when the value comes from a child table); mapped dimensions: {2}.

data.name: IDS_PERMISSION_SOURCE_DUPLICATED
data.value: The permission code source has already been specified; it can only be specified once.

data.name: IDS_VALIDATION_FAILED_SINGLE
data.value: Permission model registration validation failed.

data.name: IDS_VALIDATION_FAILED_MULTIPLE
data.value: Permission model registration validation failed with {0} problems:

data.name: IDS_MODEL_INSTANTIATE_FAILED
data.value: Failed to instantiate the permission model: {0}

data.name: IDS_DECISION_NULL_RESOURCE
data.value: Resource is null; cannot make a decision (fail-closed)

data.name: IDS_DECISION_UNMODELED
data.value: No permission model registered; not constrained by data scope

data.name: IDS_COMMON_NONE
data.value: (none)

data.name: IDS_DECISION_SUMMARY
data.value: Decision: {0}; scope key: {1}; matched allows: {2}; matched denies: {3}

data.name: IDS_DECISION_ALLOW
data.value: allow

data.name: IDS_DECISION_DENY
data.value: deny

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_DIMENSION_EXPRESSION_UNSUPPORTED
data.value: The value expression '{1}' of dimension '{0}' is not supported. A collection dimension only supports the shape "a navigation collection of the resource (optionally filtered by Where) then its string value", for example x => x.Members.Select(m => m.UserId), x => x.Members.Where(m => m.Status == "active").Select(m => m.UserId), or x => x.MemberIds when the element itself is a string; every other shape can not be pushed down into an EXISTS sub-query and is therefore rejected here. Use Map for a single value that lives on the row itself.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_NOT_PROVIDED
data.value: No policy was provided. The policy and the model must be written in the same declaring type; validation can not pass when either one is missing.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_CODE_WITHOUT_POLICY
data.value: Permission code '{0}' was declared but no policy was provided for it.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_CODE_NEVER_RESOLVED
data.value: A row-level policy was declared for permission code '{0}', but no operation resolves to that code (please check that the codes on [Permission] match the codes in Declare). Resolved codes: {1}.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_NEVER_ALLOW
data.value: The policy can never allow structurally (Allow is constantly false), which usually means every branch under Any is a deny condition. Please check the composition of the policy.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_MULTIPLE_MODELS_FOR_TYPE
data.value: Resource type '{0}' has more than one permission model (another one is '{1}'). Please make sure each resource type declares exactly one permission model.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_SUBJECT_RESOLVER_MISSING
data.value: Data scope is enabled (a scope model or a [Permission] declaration exists) but {0} is not registered. Please provide an implementation backed by authorization data in the service registrations.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_GUARD_NOT_RESOLVED
data.value: The resource type is constrained by data scope, but {0} can not be resolved from the scope of the object. Please make sure AddPermission has been called.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_POLICY_SNAPSHOT_UNSTABLE
data.value: Scope policy compilation still could not obtain a stable authorization-data snapshot after {0} attempts; concurrent Refresh calls keep occurring. Please check for code that repeatedly calls IScopeGuard.Refresh within the same scope.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_RESOLVE_UNSTABLE
data.value: Authorization-data resolution still was not accepted after {0} attempts; concurrent Refresh calls keep occurring. Please check for code that repeatedly calls IScopeGuard.Refresh within the same scope.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_EMPTY_SUBJECT_READONLY
data.value: {0}.{1} is a shared read-only instance and can not have grants added; call Clone() first when a mutable copy is needed.

data.name: IDS_SCOPE_SUBCOLLECTION_NOT_LOADED
data.value: Data scope evaluation failed: the child table dimension '{0}' of resource type '{1}' (value source: {2}) is unavailable during single row evaluation — the corresponding child collection is not loaded (null reference). Single row evaluation computes the same expression tree in memory and needs a complete object graph; because an undecidable result is a failure, this throws instead of silently denying. How to fix: ① use IScopeGuard.Apply for pushdown on the read side (EXISTS on the database side, recommended); ② load the child collection together with the object (for example Include in EF Core); ③ remove the initializer of the collection property (for example = []) — otherwise "not loaded" turns into "empty collection" and is silently denied.
